messages:
alex.t: heads up — mypy is failing on autogen pydantic models for optional nested fields in the Python SDK (v0.12.4). error says: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type 'str | None', variable has type 'str')

marie: ugh, can you paste a tiny repro?

alex.t: repro below (super reduced):
```py
from sdk import GeneratedModel

m = GeneratedModel.from_dict({
  'id': 123,
  'metadata': None,
})

reveal_type(m.metadata)  # shows 'str' not 'str | None' in mypy
```

sam: which generator did you use? autogen-cli or openapi->pydantic?

alex.t: autogen-cli (the one we run in CI to produce models). generator.yaml: uses `allow_none: true` for some fields but type annotation in generated model ends up as `str` instead of `Optional[str]`.

jordan: confirming I saw similar with nested unions — mypy/pyright disagree when using `Union[str, None]` vs `Optional[str]` in stubs. pyright tolerates it but mypy flags assignment issues depending on how pydantic parses default_factory.

ryan: quick workaround: cast the field in caller: `m.metadata = cast(Optional[str], m.metadata)` or change reveal_type to `Optional[str]`. but we should fix generator. :hammer: :bug: 

marie: I dug in — generator templates for pydantic models are emitting `metadata: str = Field(...)` when the schema has `nullable: true` only if `x-nullable` flag set, otherwise it incorrectly treats `nullable` as runtime-only. Patch idea: update Jinja template to use `Optional[{{type}}]` whenever `nullable` or `allow_none` true. Also add tests in repo `tests/typing/` to run mypy on generated models.

alex.t: that sounds right. can we add a mypy check to the autogen pipeline in CI so regressions fail fast?

devx-bot: CI job triggered: `autogen-mypy-check` (status: queued)

sam: note: there's another class of failures — streaming async client methods return `AsyncIterator[Token]` at runtime but the stubs say `Iterator[Token]` (sync). Leads to `Incompatible return type` in pyright for async functions. generator currently uses same template for sync/async. We need separate templates or conditional types: `AsyncIterator` vs `Iterator`.

marie: good catch. propose adding a small mapping in the generator: if method.async: use `typing.AsyncIterator` and annotate `async def stream(...) -> AsyncIterator[Token]:` ; else `def stream(...) -> Iterator[Token]:`. I'll open a PR.

alex.t: can you also make generated overloads for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints? sometimes clients expose both sync `.stream()` and `.stream_async()` wrappers. Overload helps mypy understand usage.

ryan: PR reference for a related fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/234 — I opened a draft that updates pydantic template + adds mypy tests.

marie: thanks. quick note on pyright: it sometimes resolves `Optional[...]` vs `Union[..., None]` differently in cross-module cases. To be conservative, generator should use `Optional[...]` consistently (PEP recommended readable form).

sam: small compatibility concern: some users run pydantic v1 in their envs while we generate code targeting pydantic v2. The type signatures between v1/v2 can differ (BaseModel parse_obj return types). We should add a generator flag `target_pydantic_version` and branch templates accordingly.

marie: agreed. added to PR checklist. Also adding changelog entry and a migration note in SDK release notes.

alex.t: temporary local patch I used (for anyone blocked): edit generated model and replace `metadata: str` with `metadata: Optional[str]` and add `from typing import Optional`. Works until PR lands.

jordan: let's also add a tiny lint in devex that scans for `: None` in union types and fails. small but painful to debug later.

marie: assigning to @marie to shepherd the autogen PR, target milestone `0.13.1`. I'll coordinate with infra to land CI mypy job in `ci/autogen.yml`.

alex.t: thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. ping me if you want a hand writing tests. :+1:

ryan: leaving a :eyes: reaction.

devx-bot: PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/234 (draft) — added to channel for visibility.

sam: final note — we should add a small README section in `docs/devex/typing.md` describing common typing pitfalls for SDK consumers (streaming, optional fields, pydantic v1 vs v2). saved multiple hours across teams.

marie: agreed, will add after PR merges. closing this thread once PR is green.
